description: Product Description

The cornerstone of our Fair Trade Organic line - FTO House Blend is a satisfying blend of medium and dark roasts. Deep, rich and full-bodied. Certified Organic and Fair Trade.This is predominately an American coffee, and perhaps that's why the flavors come together so harmoniously. It's like subtle shades of the same palette (or palate, if you choose) with complementary flavor notes that don't compete for attention. Typical of a breakfast blend it's a lighter roast; however, it doesn't have alarmingly bright, teeth-tingling acidity. It's got balance, and warmth, and certainly enough vitality and vibrancy to be a breakfast blend. While we've developed this blend to be a favorite first taste of the day, a great many of us enjoy drinking this blend throughout the day.
About the Brand

In 1981, Green Mountain Coffee Roasters hung its shingle on the front of a small cafe in Waitsfield, Vermont. This cafe roasted coffee on the premises and formed the base of operations for what was to become one of the nation's leading specialty coffee companies.

The demand for high-quality, freshly roasted coffee soon grew beyond the cafe's walls. Restaurants and inns in the area asked for coffee and equipment. Green Mountain Coffee Roasters was soon in the wholesale business to satisfy these requests. Before long, skiers asked if the cafe could send Green Mountain Coffee to their homes in New York, Florida, Pennsylvania, or Connecticut. This demand was filled by the birth of the company's mail-order business.

Green Mountain Coffee's Committment "Green Mountain Coffee Roasters is about more than making coffee, we are about committment. A committment that every sip will reflect our passion for the art of roasting coffee. We will always strive to protect the ecosystems where our coffees are harvested, and that you will always be completely satisfied with our products."

Next, he produced a Sangiovese and sold 672 bottles to the Anne Rice Fan Club in New Orleans. He was in business. By 1995, the blood of the vine began to stealthily trickle through New York and small pockets of America, becoming a prized possession. Sales grew to over half a million bottles per year. In 2011, Vampire Lounge & Tasting Room in Beverly Hills opened to proudly showcase Vampire wines. Towering mountains give rise to complex soils producing grapes with rich varietal flavors. Marine-cooled terrains allow for a long, cool growing season and for the all-important hang time to produce fruit with inherent balance, complexity and good acidity. Vampire wines celebrate the art of winemaking and creative branding to promote popular culture's fascination with vampires. During spring the bushes beautify everything around with their gentle flowers, while in the autumn they give us these small red fruits, packed with the summer sun’s energy and a combination of useful ingredients. The rose hips (Rosa canina fruits) contain extremely high amounts of vitamin C. For comparison, 100 g of fresh lemon contains 53 mg, whereas in 100 g of rose hips the average amount of vitamin C found is about 500 mg. Besides vitamin C, rose hips contain high amounts of vitamin A (about 7 mg in 100 gr of fruit) and essential fatty acids (Omega-3 and Omega-6). description: For centuries, people all over the world have preserved vegetables using fermentation that begins simply by adding salt. The resulting fermentation creates a by-product, lactic acid, which gives the resulting vegetable (here cabbage to sauerkraut) its characteristically tangy flavor. The lactic acid also helps preserve the product so that it can be enjoyed later. Still, the resulting â€œsour cabbageâ€ or â€œsauerkrautâ€ will not last beyond a few months without being hot-packed and sealed in an air-tight container. Hot-packing also stops the fermentation process right at the optimal moment to deliver a consistently delicious crispy sauerkraut. description: Our Honey Mustard Powder is a versatile all-around seasoning blend. With an ensemble cast of herbs and spices supporting the classic, time-honored combination of honey and mustard, this seasoning blend fuses sweet and savory notes with just a little sour and a touch of heat.

We wanted to put a different spin on traditional honey mustard, which is often simply honey plus mustard. And while classics are classics for a reason, that doesn’t mean they don’t leave any room to be improved upon. We added maple sugar to create a sweet flavor with depth and complexity, then contrasted that with the bold, umami-laden backbone of tamari soy sauce powder to make the flavors pop. The sunny earthiness of turmeric adds balance to pert cider vinegar, which cuts a sour path through the deeper flavors and elevates everything along the way.

Try Honey Mustard Powder tossed over hot wings. Coat pork in Honey Mustard Powder when you make some Honey Balsamic Pork Chops. Add complex flavor to classic condiments by stirring into red wine vinegar and olive oil for a quick and easy vinaigrette. Pour over roasted potatoes for an easy, non-dairy potato salad. Sprinkle over pretzels or peanuts and bake for a fun snack, or combine with sour cream and cream cheese for a dip for pretzels, fresh veggies, or chicken fingers.

All ingredients at Spice Enthusiast are packaged fresh daily by hand, and delivered to your door in a heat-sealed, resealable, recyclable Kraft bag for optimal freshness and shelf-life. Store your ingredients in a dry, dark, and cool location.

About the Brand

There really is a "yogi" behind Yogi Tea. In 1969, Yogi Bhajan began teaching Kundalini Yoga in America, sharing the ancient wisdom of Ayurveda and healthy living that he had mastered in India. After each class, he would serve his students a special spice tea based upon this healing science, which they affectionately named Yogi Tea. Soon, Yogi Bhajan’s students opened Golden Temple Vegetarian Restaurants in the US, Canada, and Europe. The delicious, rich and spicy aroma of Yogi Tea brewing permeated the environment and every customer who enjoyed the tea wanted to make their own cup of Yogi Tea at home. Through these Golden Temple restaurants, the first batches of Yogi Tea were sold to the public. In 1984, this grassroots endeavor blossomed into The Yogi Tea Company and Yogi Tea began to appear on Natural Foods Store shelves throughout the country.

Today, Yogi Tea makes a rich beverage line of 13 Exotic Teas from all over the world that includes the original spice formula, now called Classic India Spice, plus Healing Formulas, Woman’s Healing Formulas, Green Tea Healing Formulas, Green Teas, and several flavors of Organic Chai. Organic ingredients, Ayurvedic wisdom, and modern knowledge are incorporated into every product they develop at their modern manufacturing facility in Eugene, Oregon. In their own words: "We are committed to applying our yogic lifestyle to our businesses, honoring diversity and the need for individuals to grow in social and spiritual ways."

features: Made from grade one (the highest grade) premium broad tea leaves from the very first Spring harvest.

description: Sometime during China's Tang Dynasty, about 1300 years ago, it was noticed that broad leaf teas transported from Yunnan Province (along what is known as the "Tea Horse Road") to China's then capital city, Chang'an, Tibet and other destinations, underwent a unique transformation during the long journeys. The taste of the brew from these tea leaves actually became smoother and more distinctive. This tea, known as Pu-erh tea, became highly sought-after by the Tang Court, the literati and the nobility. Pu-erh tea came to be known as the "King of Tea" for good reason. High quality Pu-erh is still in great demand by tea connoisseurs and is one of the few teas that, like wine, improves and becomes smoother over time. There are two types of Pu-erh tea: Ripe Pu-erh is tea that has undergone an accelerated fermentation process while Raw Pu-erh has not and is/has been allowed to undergo natural fermentation over time. Bana Tea Limited Edition 2008 Vintage tea was harvested from 100 to 400-year old tea trees from Jinggu Mountain, Simao Prefecture in China's Yunnan Province. Made from grade one tea (the highest grade of tea), these leaves brew into a peach-yellow concoction with a crisp delicate dried apricot flavor. The aroma of this raw tea is both refreshing and stimulating. Bana Tea Limited Edition 2008 Vintage tea normally is manufactured in traditional 200 gram tea cakes. This beautifully-designed box contains 50 grams of the grade one tea that has been segmented into convenient ready-to-brew portions. It is a good tea to enjoy in the morning or when you need a brief hiatus from a hectic routine.

Packaged For Freshness: At Raven's Brew, we take freshness seriously. Our coffee is packaged shortly after roasting, in air-tight bags, with one-way valves that seal in the incredible aromas and flavors. Our packaging protects your coffee from the light and air, which are both major contributors to stale coffee.

High-Quality Beans, Perfectly Roasted: We choose rare, high-quality beans from some of the world’s best coffee plantations and delicately roast them to create super smooth layers of flavor. Our process creates a strong, rich and flavorful coffee—perfectly smooth with no unpleasant acidity.

Sustainable And Kind To The Environment: We support small family growers through our coffee buying practices. Not just because they make the best coffee, but because it’s the right thing to do.

Used by cooks worldwide when seasoning their favorite foods, Fleur de Sel is one of the most treasured finishing salts for gourmet dishes, adding subtle salinity and crunch, and in spice & herb blends, as it helps to break down herbs and open up their flavor.

description: Brazil Cerrado Coffee Beans: 100% Arabica and the highest grade of the famous Brazilian beans, lively and inviting with a smooth, sweet taste. Beans from the Cerrado region have cupped better than those from the Santos region. Cerrado is a huge region in Brazil, meaning "savanna", or central plateau. Coffee grown in this region is cultivated at an altitude of 200-500 meters above sea level--quite a bit lower than our Strictly Hard Bean (SHB) Central American Coffees. Because Cerrado is a softer bean, some roasters think it shouldn't be roasted overly dark. Other Roasters thinks Cerrado should be roasted dark, but watch out for scorching. Dark roasting brings out an exceptional nutty flavor and enhances the body of the coffee. Our Cerrado is a traditionally natural dry processed coffee. This method creates a complexity of flavors. Brazilian coffees make excellent bases for some very intriguing blends, particularly in espresso. A lot of the very best espresso blends have a Brazilian base. Many of the finest Italian espresso blends are mostly Brazilian coffee. It will add body and sweetness to your blend, and helps form a wonderful crema in your espresso. Since it is a dry processed coffee, it may roast a bit unevenly, but this only adds to the complexity in the cup. It actually makes a fine cup on it's own.

description: Product Description

Pure ceylon tea. The Story of Tea: In the mountains along the Equator grows an evergreen shrub with 5 petal blossoms, which resemble wild white roses. Legend has it that as far back as 2737 B.C. Emperor Chen Nug of China used to boil the leaves of this remarkable shrub in water and drank the infusion - thus beginning the ceremonious art of drinking tea. It then quickly spread to Japan and eventually to England all of Europe. Bentley's Finest Teas are coveted by tea lovers everywhere for their full bodied fragrance and exquisite taste, the result of using only the purest ingredients available along with Ceylon's finest harvesting and processing techniques. Bentley's - Appreciated by Connoisseurs The World Over. Imported & distributed in the USA. Pure Ceylon Tea - Packed in Sri Lanka.
About the Brand

Bentley's Tea are distributed by the Boston Tea Company, founded in 1949. Boston Tea Company was the first to market flavored teas with the introduction of its Boston's Mint-in-Tea, a delightful blend of orange pekoe tea and Kentucky spearmint. In 1960, the company introduced and was granted a trademark for its "Boston Tea Party" blend, which re-created a popular blend that dates back to the colonists in the 1770s. This product is a blend of fine black teas blended with orange peels and cloves--also known as orange spice tea. This product was a favorite of the first lady, Jacqueline Kennedy, who served it frequently to White House guests.

During the 1970s, when specialty teas became increasingly popular, Boston Tea Company broadened their line considerably. Today, they are the industry leader in marketing flavored and gourmet teas in decorative and reusable canisters. Boston Tea Company is based in Hackensack, New Jersey.

description: There's much to love about Brazil nut, besides their generous size and creamy taste. Of all the nuts, they take the prize for having the most intriguing backstory (do tell!).

Here goes: Brazil nuts are seeds that grow in ponderous pods-we're talking over five pounds, each one containing as many as two dozen seeds-on these towering trees that can grow to 160 feet high and live as long as 500 years. During the harvest season, these pods will let loose and fall to the ground at the rate of about 50 miles an hour. Then the real fun begins, since it requires a pretty powerful axe to crack open the tough shell-or the services of the agouti, the only animal with the mandibles to gnaw right through.

What really makes Brazil nuts so exceptional, though, is that they are mostly harvested from trees that still grow in the wild, with just a small smattering farmed on plantations. And get this: There's only one insect that's up to the job of pollinating the supersized seeds, and that's the poetically named orchid bee. It just doesn't get more authentic than that. You'll never chomp on a Brazil nut the same way again.

description: Ben & Jerry's Caramel Chocolate Cheesecake.... In your cheesecake dreams is it like you’re spooning through a world of caramel cheesecake ice cream swirled with chocolate cookies in a wonderland of truffles filled with cheesecake. Hello. You can wake up now… It’s no secret that we love cheesecake here at Ben & Jerry’s. We’ve found an excuse to make it our anchor flavor in any number of concoctions but here’s a little secret: While we love the tangy sweetness of cheesecake we’re equally enamored with its graham-cracker sidekick. There’s just something about that sweet and slightly crunchy combo that gets us right in our Ooey gooey hearts every time with this frozen treat. Luckily we’re not the only ones who go gaga for grahams around here. So when we discovered that we could double the cheesecake ratio by infusing caramel cheesecake ice cream with cheesecake truffles rolled in graham crackers we were all in. When topped off with a chocolate-cookie swirl there’s not much better than Chocolate Caramel Cheesecake for dreamy creamy graham-cracker-y scheming. With Fairtrade-certified sugar cocoa and vanilla at the core non-GMO ingredients and cage-free eggs we’re proud to stand behind the ingredients used to make this cheesecake dream a reality. Ben & Jerrys will be your new favorite homemade ice cream.

features: Cloves are used in the cuisine of Asian, African, and the Near and Middle East countries, lending flavor to meats, curries, and marinades, as well as fruit such as apples, pears or rhubarb.
Cloves may be used to give aromatic and flavor qualities to hot beverages, often combined with other ingredients such as lemon and sugar.

In Mexican cuisine, cloves are best known as clavos de olor, and often accompany cumin and cinnamon. They are also used in Peruvian cuisine, in a wide variety of dishes as carapulcra and arroz con leche.
Cloves are used in Indian Ayurvedic medicine, Chinese medicine, and western herbalism and dentistry where the essential oil is used as an anodyne (painkiller) for dental emergencies.
Cloves are used as a carminative, to increase hydrochloric acid in the stomach and to improve peristalsis.
description: Cloves are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum. They are native to the Maluku Islands in Indonesia, and are commonly used as a spice. Cloves are commercially harvested primarily in Bangladesh, Indonesia, India, Madagascar, Zanzibar, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Tanzania. Cloves are available throughout the year.

About the Brand
Ahmad Tea of London draws upon knowledge and experience gained from three generations of family activity in all areas of the tea trade, from plantations to blending and packaging.

The name of Ahmad Tea is synonymous with the very finest teas. Our expert tea tasters have sampled teas from many gardens around the world in search of suitable tea leaves to make the perfect cup. After careful selection, traditional methods of hand plucking ensure that the tea arrives in perfect condition, with the freshness and flavour intact. The leaves are then meticulously blended to meet our high standards of quality and consistency. Teas can only be used after the Director of Tea Tasting has personally tasted each blend and approved it for production. The result is an excellent cup of tea, with impeccable liquor, colour, aroma and flavour.

The company was established with the belief that our reputation must be founded on the quality of our teas. The commitment to quality remains today. It is reflected in the image, branding and packaging of the entire Ahmad Tea product range and has led to sales in more than forty-five countries, spanning across five continents.
Ahmad Tea is based in Hampshire, England, with a US office in Deer Park, Texas.

About the Brand

Everyone asks, "How did a social worker and a psychologist, fresh out of graduate school, get into the snack food business?" The social worker, Stacy Madison and the psychologist, Mark Andrus shared a passion for good food and a commitment to staying healthy. Here's their story: "We decided to open a downtown Boston restaurant. However, large student loans and no capital halted our dream. So we decided to take a risk. We designed a food cart and began serving healthy pita bread roll-up sandwiches. They were an instant hit and the lines grew longer each day. As an incentive for customers to wait in line, we baked fresh pita bread into different flavored chips. Customers loved them so much, they encouraged us to get the chips into stores. We listened, and that's how Stacy's Pita Chip Company was born. Thanks to our loyal customers, our chips are now available nationwide."

description: About the Brand

Lipton is the world's best-known and best-selling brand of tea, and is the global market leader in both leaf and ready-to-drink tea, with a global market share nearly three times larger than its nearest rival. Available in more than 110 countries, Lipton is particularly popular in Europe, North America, and the Middle East and parts of Asia.
Lipton is a member of the Unilever family of brands.

About UnileverUnilever brands are trusted everywhere; in fact, 150 million times a day, someone somewhere chooses a Unilever product. Among its many well-known food brands are Bestfoods, Knorr, Birds Eye, Bertolli, Lipton, and Ben & Jerry's. Many of its home care and personal care products are market leaders, including Brilhante, Cif, Comfort, Dove, Lux, Pond's, Rexona and Sunsilk. In other words, look in your refrigerator, freezer, or bathroom cabinet, and you're likely to find a Unilever product.

In the 1890s, William Hesketh Lever, founder of Lever Bros., wrote down his ideas for Sunlight Soap--his revolutionary new product that helped popularize cleanliness and hygiene in Victorian England. His idea was "to make cleanliness commonplace; to lessen work for women; to foster health and contribute to personal attractiveness, that life may be more enjoyable and rewarding for the people who use our products." This was long before the phrase "Corporate Mission" had been invented, but these ideas have continued to guide the practices of Unilever ever since, even if Lever's language and the notion of only women doing housework has become outdated.

In the late 19th century, the businesses that would later become Unilever were among the most philanthropic of their time. They set up projects to improve the lot of their workers and created products with a positive social impact, making hygiene and personal care commonplace and improving nutrition through adding vitamins to foods that were already daily staples. Today, Unilever still believes that success means, as its corporate principles state, acting with "the highest standards of corporate behavior towards our employees, consumers and the societies and world in which we live." Over the years the company has launched or participated in an ever-growing range of initiatives to source sustainable supplies of raw materials, protect environments, support local communities, and much more.

Just like you would any delicious, smooth tea: hot or iced. It’s even great in protein shakes. Use it while studying, working, exercising, living!

description: Description: Tonka beans are the seeds found in the fruit of the tropical kumarú tree or Dipteryx odorata, a tree very tall as it can reach up to 30 meters. The tree grows throughout South America, is found mainly in Venezuela, Guyana and Brazil. Tonka in the language of the native Galibi of French Guiana means "bean" and the kumarú tree is botanically classified as legumes (Fabaceae). The tonka bean is black and looks like corrugated almond. The aroma of tonka bean has also been used in the preparation of perfumes. It is reminiscent of vanilla, almonds, cinnamon, cloves, caramel and tobacco. It tastes like bitter almond and at the same time has a similar taste to caramel, chocolate and vanilla. The beans are used in very small quantities to flavor meat dishes, various soufflés, sweets, syrups, ice creams and cocktails. They are also widely used in French cuisine, and are popular with top patissiers for elaborate desserts, usually in combination with creams.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description: A unique Arabica variety of coffee! Catimor is the "fourth bean" that helps give Vietnamese blends their unparalleled complexity. In Vietnam, Catimor is rarely given center stage, though. In Nicaragua, on the other hand, Catimor is a prized heirloom. The result is a premium quality bean with a unique and deeply layered flavor profile. The farm uses mandarin orange trees as shade trees, too, which adds to the sweet citrusy fragrance.After extensive experimentation we chose this coffee for our cold brew and Blonde roasts, dubbing the Blonde roast Limoncello due to its pleasing fruity, lemony profile. In many Arabicas lemon notes are a fault, as they accompany an overly-high acidity. But in this Matagalpa-region Catimor, acidity is 40% lower than most Arabicas, so the lemon tone is more of a lemon zest note than lemon sour. Incredibly refreshing as an iced drink or espresso.

description: Product Description

CalPure Avocado Oil is quickly becoming one of the most exciting ingredients in the pantry today. Pale in color and mild in flavor, this naturally-refined avocado oil provides a blank canvas for whatever spices and sauces are being added to a dish. Since the time the Aztecs, the avocado has been prized for its many health benefits and nutrients, particularly its monounsaturated fats, high in cholesterol-lowering beta sitosterol. That’s what makes CalPure Avocado Oil the perfect addition to any heart-healthy diet. In addition, this oil’s remarkably high smoke point makes it ideal for medium to very high-heat cooking up to 520°F. As the only cooking oil made from the pulp of the fruit rather than the pit, avocado oil is produced as naturally as possible, free of hexane and other chemical solvents used in the extraction process of so many other cooking oils.
From the Manufacturer
Provides a Blank Canvas for Your Culinary Creations
Neutral in color and flavor, naturally-refined avocado oil readily adapts the flavors you are cooking with, allowing you to taste your food, not your cooking oil.
Highest Smoke Point of Any Cooking Oil

No more smoking pans and bitter tasting food. CalPure Avocado Oil is naturally-refined for safe and effective high-heat cooking up to 520°F. Grilling, searing and frying food to perfection is an art, but using a cooking oil that is appropriate for high-heat cooking makes a big difference.
Perfect Compliment to a Healthy Diet

Since the time the Aztecs, the avocado has been prized for its many health benefits and nutrients. Like avocados themselves, avocado oil is high in heart-healthy, cholesterol lowering monounsaturated fats, making it the perfect addition to any healthy diet, including the Mediterranean diet.
Naturally-Refined Using Premium Avocados
As the only cooking oil made from the pulp of the fruit, avocado oil is produced without the use of hexane and other chemical solvents. CalPure Avocado Oil is also naturally Non-GMO.
Incredibly Versatile

CalPure Avocado Oil is neutral in flavor and has the highest smoke point of any cooking oil, making it the perfect go-to oil. What’s more, it provides a blank canvas for your favorite sauces, dressings and vinaigrettes.
CalPure Foods

On our family farm in Central California, we grow only the best and safest produce. We love cooking and take the same extraordinary care in providing healthy, high quality foods to our customers around the world.
About the Startup
Describe your product in 3 words.
Favorite, Healthy, Affordable
How did you come up with the idea for this product?

As avid home cooks and California vegetable farmers, we wanted to find a healthy, versatile cooking oil that we could use to make our favorite dishes for friends and family, including our two young children. In 2015 we opened a cold-pressing facility in Southern California and began making our own extra virgin avocado oil. In late 2015 we added naturally-refined avocado oil to our lineup. This oil has a permanent home on our kitchen counter and find ourselves reaching for it as a daily, all-purpose cooking oil and baking ingredient. We hope it will find a home on your counter too!
What makes your product special?

We love naturally-refined avocado oil because of its high smoke point and unlimited applications. We are excited to introduce a healthy replacement for canola & vegetable oil that is made without hexanes or other chemical solvents that are standard in the extraction process of so many other cooking oils.
What has been the best part of your startup experience?
The most rewarding part of our experience is creating products we are all proud of and truly believe in.

description: Product Description

Billington's Natural Dark Brown Molasses Sugar is a soft, moist, decadent gourmet sugar. Rich in the cane's inherent molasses, Dark Brown Molasses Sugar is the darkest of all our sugars. It's gloriously deep in color with a sticky texture. It has a rich aroma and great depth of indulgent fudge-like flavor. Try it in savory BBQ sauces, balsamic vinaigrette, and tomato sauces such as bolognaise. Billington's has a flavor character which marries well with rich chocolate recipes... We recommend it for gooey brownies, decadent fudge, holiday cakes, and chocolate chip cookies. Use as a 1-for-1 replacement for brown sugar. Billington’s Unrefined Cane Sugars are unlike any sugar you will ever taste. The secret to Billington’s remarkable flavor is the molasses. Many brown sugars are only brown on the outside and made by coating refined white sugar in molasses. Unlike conventional brown sugars on the market, Billington’s still holds a bit of the cane’s natural molasses within each glistening crystal. Our Dark Brown Molasses Sugar is made simply ... with the aim of locking in, not refining out, the sugar cane's natural molasses. Produced naturally on the island of Mauritius, Billington’s gourmet sugars bring centuries of tradition into each sparking crystal. Mauritius has a unique combination of climate, soil conditions and tropical sun that is perfectly suited to growing sugar cane unmatched in quality.
About the Brand

Based in Peterborough, UK, Billington's has been importing sugars for over 140 years to become Europe's leading supplier of unrefined cane sugars. Billington's pioneered the market for high-quality unrefined sugars and was the first to source a certified-organic cane sugar for the UK market.

The company now offers one of the most comprehensive ranges of natural and unrefined organic cane sugars in Europe. The name Billington's is synonymous with the very best in brown and golden sugars; they source and market the best unrefined sugars from expert suppliers across the world.

description: Bodhi Leaf first offered coffees from Rio Jorco over 4 years ago. This Caturra varietal shows exceptional depth and the honey process has really brought out its best attributes. Notes of black cherry, vanilla cola, dark chocolate and molasses really encompass just how sweet and syrupy this coffee is! “Hacienda Jorco, now known as Rio Jorco S.A., is rich in history and played a key role in the development of the Jorco- Acosta region all based on the proceeds of the sale of his excellent quality coffee. In the early 1900's two families by the name of Challe and Briote had a small farm and beneficio (processing plant) near where the present Rio Jorco micro-beneficio is currently located. On finishing his Schooling in Agriculture at a University in Cuba, a young Jorge Zeledon returned to his native Costa Rica seeking employment. He was hired as the farm manager for the small coffee operation. After working there for two years, the family offered to sell don Jorge the processing plant and farm. Young Jorge expressed his dismay at not having the funds to buy the farm. ‘No problem’ said the owners, ‘just pay us from the proceeds of the coffee.’ He agreed and was blessed with very good coffee harvests and prices which allowed him to go from a 20 acre coffee operation to over a thousand acre farm that was the largest in the area. He married early to Claudia and they had 6 girls living in the large farmhouse in Jorco and in his San Jose home about 15 miles away. In its eary history, the coffee from the farm had to be taken from Jorco to San Jose using Oxen or on horseback. Thought the distance was only about 15 miles it was a long trip up winding muddy roads. It required oxen to be changed 2 or three times and a one day trip was considered fast. The dedication and passion for fine coffee is carried out today by Luis and Jim Alfaro, grandkids of the founder and sons of his daughter Cavita.”

description: At Diamond of California, we have offered fresh, high quality and great tasting nuts for over 100 years since we were founded by a group of walnut growers in 1912. From whole or chopped to sliced or slivered, we offer a wide range of chop types and varieties of nuts—both in and out of their shells. This includes shelled and in-shell walnuts, pecans, almonds, black walnuts, macadamias, pine nuts, Brazil nuts, hazelnuts, cashews and pistachios. Diamond Nuts are all unseasoned and ready for baking, cooking, snacking or even adding as a topping. We believe that adding nuts makes good food even better!

Toasting nuts adds extra flavor and crispness. For best results, we recommend toasting in the oven or on the stovetop. Nuts toasted in the microwave do not develop as much flavor or crunch. Toasting time depends on both the size and variety of the nut.
Oven Toasting:

Spread nuts in a single layer on an ungreased baking pan. Place in a 350°F oven and bake 5 to 12 minutes or until nuts are golden brown; stir once or twice until toasty and fragrant. Remove from pan to cool. Nuts will continue to brown slightly after removed from oven.
Stove-Top Toasting:
Place nuts in a heavy skillet over medium heat and stir or toss continuously until nuts turn a golden brown and smell toasty and fragrant, approximately 3 to 8 minutes.
Microwave Toasting:
Spread nuts in a single layer in a glass pie plate. Microwave on HIGH 5 to 6 minutes (check frequently; microwave ovens vary), stirring every 2 minutes. Cool.

description: Product Description
An endless pursuit for the cleanest, purest cup of coffee on earth
From the Manufacturer
No-GMOs
Anyone can enjoy our coffess, with no GMOs, we're ensuring that everything we put in your cup is made at the highest standards.
Certified Organic
Limitless Coffee is Organic, Direct Trade coffee. We relentlessly pursue the cleanest, purest beans — Certified Koser, Certified Organic, wet-washed, air roasted, and Gluten-Free.
Select the Farm

We have traveled all over the world and work directly with farms all over the world, but choose to work with only those with organic farming practices. We have been to Central America, South America, Indonesia and Africa in search of the best farms in the world to buy from.
Import Clean Beans

Once we have found a farm, we ensure that all beans they provide us are wet washed. Wet Washed beans are beans that have been picked right from the coffee tree, immediately rinsed with clean water, de-pulped and soaked overnight. The resulting bean is almost free of contaminants.
Air Roasted

Once the beans arrive to our Roastery, we use an air roaster to remove the chaff and additional contaminants, removing more of the “harsh, bitter” taste found in coffees traditionally roasted. Air roasting eliminates the carbonization and smoke that normally burns and leaves deposits on all other beans.
Drink Cleaner Coffee

We’re always pursuing a better, cleaner way for people to drink coffee and tea. We strive in being innovative, powering people through their day, and helping people become a better version of themselves.

description: Paradise Fruit Company was incorporated in 1961 as part of Canaveral Utilities and Development Co., a land development operation on the east coast of Florida. The name "Paradise", a label used by a company that had been in the 'glace' (candied) fruit business since the end of WW2, was acquired by Canaveral during the year of incorporation. After several acquisitions and mergers with similar businesses, 'glace' fruit became the major segment of the company's business. In 1965, the name was changed to Paradise Fruit Company, Inc. During those years, there were a number of relatively small operations manufacturing candied fruit, primarily for sale to commercial bakers. The management of Paradise anticipated that there was a great potential for direct sales to homemakers through supermarkets. Over a period of several years, Paradise developed the now familiar transparent, reusable plastic containers found in almost every supermarket during the holiday season. In order to become more immediately responsive to its customers needs, the company invested in a facility to manufacture all of its packaging. This, combined with large inventories, enabled almost overnight filling and shipping of orders. During the same period, the company acquired, merged with, or was licensed by a number of competitors to become the leading marketer of 'glace' fruit products under labels that have been trusted and asked for by customers for generations. Given the increasing diversification, the name of the company was changed to Paradise, Inc. in 1993. Paradise remains an innovator in 'glace' fruit marketing, introducing in 2003 a new package design that incorporates recipes and a cash-redeemable coupon.

IMMUNITY: The water-soluble plant-polysaccharides in spelt organic flour serve as immune-stimulants. These properties help promote healthy cells.

description: Ancient Grains Whole Grain Spelt Flour

Our farming industry and the American consumer has overlooked Spelt wheat (dinkel) for decades. As a result, we have not seen the same attempts to modify or enhance commercial viability of this grain. The degree of gluten in Spelt has not changed in response to overwhelming demand.
St. Hildegard Spelt Flour

Today, the composition of farro grain and spelt grains remain consistent with their ancient form during Hildegard of Bingen's time. Like einkorn flour, Hildegard Spelt flour offers moderate gluten exposure.
Organic Spelt Wheat

Modern harvesting techniques have resolved many of the challenges related to threshing Spelt, which naturally has a tough outer shell or hull. A tough hull leaves the Spelt berry naturally better protected to grow naturally.
Ancient Grains Spelt Flour
A substantial hull protects spelt grains to grow safely. The strong hull also means the grain remains fresh and retains its nutrients longer after harvest.
Spelt Flour for Baking
Try making organic spelt bread, spelt sourdough bread, vegan spelt flour cookies, ancient grain bread pudding, roasted spelt flour, spelt tortillas, spelt flour pancakes.

description: Famous chefs and celebrity bakers know it. Now you can know it, too. There is a form of baking salt called powdered salt or flour salt. This unique salt is sodium chloride, like all other salts. But it is pulverized, ground up into super fine particle sizing. The small and fine granulation of the salt gives it the ability to season things in a way that adheres to a high surface area, with a more even salting experience. The kind of salt you use in baking also affects the texture (and elasticity) of the dough. Using fine salt flour makes your doughs stronger and less sticky-yucky-gooey. Imagine creating pizza dough you can actually handle like the pizza pros in the pizza shop – spinning the dough and hand tossing it without any sticky residue! The same holds true for your doughs for braiding or for your pie crusts. Powdered granulated salt also makes it easier for you to do a lighter application of salt seasoning for salads, popcorns and other recipes. Because the fine salt coats evenly, a bit goes further. The lighter salt sticks to the food and doesn’t lump and sink to the bottom, making this Fine Kosher Salt your secret ingredient to perfectly created cuisine. Flour salt water also creates a perfect brine with the fine particle salt blending into the water or herbed solutions perfectly. Order your Specialty Baking Salt today and begin to cook and bake like the pros do it, with this fine particle salt.

description: It’s new to North America but long a staple in the Philippines.

description: Founded in 1972, Stash Tea Company originally operated out of an old Portland Victorian style house, supplying loose herbal teas and bulk herbs to natural food stores. Starting in 1975, the company broadened its focus to include bagged teas and then began to sell a full line of traditional, specialty blend and herbal teas directly to fine restaurants and through a mail order catalog to consumers. Today, Stash Tea Company is one of the largest specialty tea companies in the United States. The company derives its name from an entertaining aspect of tea folklore. In earlier centuries, tea was a valuable commodity traditionally transported by clipper ship. The ship’s captain often was presented with some of the finest teas for his personal use. This supply was his “stash,” stowed carefully as his “private reserve.” Today, the term is still used to denote anything put away carefully because of its preciousness.

description: About the Brand

Traditionally, Classic English Tea Merchants dedicated themselves to providing high quality teas in accordance with British tea industry standards. These standards were widely accepted in the Britain of the 1800s and 1900s vigorously applied so that the good and fine teas were selected, carefully blended in the right proportions, and offered for sale on the basis of clearly defined and widely accepted grades and standards. Unfortunately, over the years, quality levels were diluted in most of the western world. In the case of America, which has been primarily a coffee drinking nation, the experience and knowledge of the tea industry was never completely developed. While the U.S. has been in the forefront of production and innovation (e.g. the teabag, iced tea), the specific skills of tasting, buying and blending teas were not well developed.

To revive these standards for todays tea consumer, a company was incorporated 6 years ago in England to revive these traditions of the original English tea merchants. Todays Harrisons & Crosfields mission is to acquire the highest quality teas and natural flavourings to provide the broadest packaged product line in the industry. This means having our London tea buyers with many years experience select the teas and carefully blend or flavour them in the British tradition. The teas are then shipped in bulk to the U.S. to utilize the innovative packaging and production techniques of the U.S. The goal is to have the finest available premium teas packaged in the form that meets the needs of todays consumer.

features: Nice mellow brightness and a very sweet tropical fruit note at the start moving into a creamy milk chocolate body with a hint of mild cherry. Hints of berry and honey throughout.
The soil, rich with volcanic ash, gives this coffee a smooth distinct body.
Hints of berry and honey throughout with a wonderful milk chocolate taste that is evident in freshly roasted coffee...yum, a very satisfying coffee treat!
The beauty of this cup really comes out well with the Pulped Natural (PN, honey processed) process.
Fresh Roasted Each Morning & Shipped in the Afternoon! Cup Characteristics: Sweet, mild cherry and creamy, luscious milk chocolate flavor nuances makes this coffee a complete and satisfying cup.
description: One of our favorites is the El Salvador, Pulped Natural or “Honey” coffee beans. The Pulped Natural Process is becoming more popular in Central America for the sweet fruit note it imparts to the cup. The beauty of this cup really comes out well with the Pulped Natural (PN, honey processed) process: you get the even roast of a wet process with the fermented darker fruit notes of a dry process. Beans are grown under variety of shade trees in ideal setting for tree maturation--constant breezes, full sunshine and relatively cool, dry nights. What sets this coffee apart is the processing:to create pulped natural, as opposed to fully washed coffees, the coffee cherry skin is removed, but instead of the sticky mucilage underneath being washed off, the beans with mucilage intact goes directly to the drying patios and is dried, raked, dried some more. This is very labor intensive as the constant raking and turning of the sticky parchment is essential. What this lends to the coffee is a brighter and sweeter finish. When all the steps are preformed correctly the results are a slight increase in sweetness, body and aromatics traditionally found in natural processed coffee, and a milder acidity than we usually find in most washed coffees.

description: Our Handcrafted, All Natural, Wood-Fired Organic Maple Syrup is produced on our Farm, located deep in the Appalachian Valley Great Lake Region of Pennsylvania. It is hand-packed for freshness and exceptional flavor at our farm. Organic Maple Products Vs. Non-Organic We always get the question “What’s not organic about Maple Syrup”? For the most part, I tend to believe that all maple syrup producers make their maple syrup with the upmost integrity. BUT there is a difference between Organic and Non- Organic maple syrup. In order for us to label our maple syrup as “Certified Organic” we had to first apply and go through a thorough inspection of all our sugarbushes, sap gathering points, neighboring lands, our sugarhouse and all equipment, our commercial kitchen areas, our handling and packaging practices, our bookkeeping methods, etc. This inspection had to be done before we were approved by OEFFA to be certified organic. This also means that we will be inspected regularly and audited. Certifying our Farm organic means that we do not use any chemicals or pesticides nor do the neighboring lands. We do not use chemicals in maple syrup tapping, production or cleaning. We do not over tap our trees. We leave a very small footprint in the sugarbush. We work very hard at producing the finest quality organic maple syrup at our farm for your table and ours.

Preparing the dough is an easy process:– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.
How to Prepare Arepas

Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cmor 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.
About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favoritecorn based recipes.

PERFECT TEXTURE: Different from our other flour types, semolina is more coarse in texture with a yellow buttery color and increased elasticity, making it the ideal pasta flour. Create perfect fresh pasta sheets with Bobs Red Mill Semolina Flour!

Bob's Red Mill Semolina flour is the chefs choice for pizza flour, this makes a fabulous pizza. Semolina is the purified milling of durum wheat. Semola is derived for the Latin word for flour, and semolina is the common name for this special flour. This ingredient adds structure and bite to homemade pasta and a small amount added to pastry dough adds a rustic character. A very necessary ingredient for Semolina bread.

It's rich in protein, fiber, and B vitamins and may support weight loss, heart health, and digestion. Most people can enjoy semolina with no issue, but a small percentage of the population may not tolerate it due to its gluten or wheat content. If you can tolerate it, try adding semolina to your diet.

Semolina flour consists of 12-13 percent protein and has a low elasticity and higher plasticity than most flour that is used for pasta. This makes semolina flour a great choice when making extruded pasta such as penne, as the shape of your pasta will not start to change as soon as it has been extruded.

description: Because the Art of Tea is about Good Taste. You deserve a moment to relax with a warm cup of tea just for yourself, or if you wish to share it with your family and friends. The recommended local practice in China for brewing the leaves is a bit more intense than the traditional gongfu method: use 5-10 grams of dry leaf for every 3-4 oz of water. Brew in either a guywan or a small teapot. Steep the first time for 20 seconds, and each additional steep at 10 seconds. Leaves can be used for 4 or 5 brews. The addition of chicory to coffee is a long-standing tradition that dates all the way back to the American Colonial Era. However, it wasn't until the American Civil War that the practice became widespread. After Union Navy blockades effectively severed trade to the ports and market of New Orleans, locals searched for ways to prolong their supply of coffee while still maintaining its taste. Chicory was hailed as the perfect substitute. Now, over a century later, the practice of drinking coffee with chicory remains a strong New Orleans tradition. Try it black or cafe au lait style with steamed milk for a true taste of New Orleans!

description: CLARIFIED SPREADABLE BUTTER 8oz

Yak butter has a rich history throughout Nepal, the Himalayas, and Mongolia. It has long been the fuel of Mt Everest climbers, taking them to the highest mountain on the planet! It is also a staple in the diets of Buddhist Monks, who sip on yak butter tea throughout the day. Traditionally salted, our unsalted yak ghee is as robust in flavor as it is healthy.

Our Yak Ghee is made from A2/A2 butter that comes from yaks living wildly roaming the vast grass plains and mountains of Mongolia. The yaks have an incredibly diverse diet of over 200 types of grasses and herbs and are herded by traditional pastoral nomads.
Certified Paleo and Keto, this new flavor is the perfect addition to your butter tea (best paired with pu-erh ) or coffee! It is also great for any recipe that calls for fat!

A2/A2 refers to the type of beta-casein protein. Most cow milk genetically contains both the A1 + A2 casein proteins, but yak milk is unique in that it only contains A2. A2/A2 milk and ghee made from it, is suggested to have less digestive issues for people sensitive to lactose or dairy.
Store in a cool, dry place. Refrigeration is optional. While clarified butter is shelf stable, use a clean utensil to avoid introducing anything foreign into the jar.
Ingredient: Full-year/pasture-raised yak butter.

features: HIGH QUALITY: 100 percent premium durum semolina flour is specially selected for quality.

BRONZE DRAWN: Specialized pasta-shaping technique resulting in unique rough texture so the sauce sticks.

description: Just about everybody enjoys pasta, but in this industrialized world, we often miss the authentic taste and texture of traditional handmade pasta, which is soft yet pleasing to chew and has just the right amount of flavor. In Apulia, Italy, known as the Italian barn, there is a small factory, where FRAMORE is bringing the passion and personal touch back to pasta. This jumbo fusilli is made with 100 percent premium durum wheat semolina flour, ground more finely than refined flour, and mixed in a mixer that is one-tenth the size that is used for industrial pasta. By using a specialized pasta-shaping technique called bronze-drawing, your fusilli will have a rougher, more porous texture, allowing any sauce or dressing to adhere to it more effectively. Their pastaio, or pasta-maker, personally takes the trays of pasta to the drying rooms, where they sit at the perfect temperature and have plenty of time to dry. This meticulous process results in perfectly replicated pasta from ancient Italian tradition, because FRAMORE cares about the details. If you want consistently al dente fusilli with delicious flavor and unwavering texture, FRAMORE is here to serve.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

About the Brand

Lipton is the world's best-known and best-selling brand of tea, and is the global market leader in both leaf and ready-to-drink tea, with a global market share nearly three times larger than its nearest rival. Available in more than 110 countries, Lipton is particularly popular in Europe, North America, and the Middle East and parts of Asia.
Lipton is a member of the Unilever family of brands.

About Unilever Unilever brands are trusted everywhere; in fact, 150 million times a day, someone somewhere chooses a Unilever product. Among its many well-known food brands are Bestfoods, Knorr, Birds Eye, Bertolli, Lipton, and Ben & Jerry's. Many of its home care and personal care products are market leaders, including Brilhante, Cif, Comfort, Dove, Lux, Pond's, Rexona and Sunsilk. In other words, look in your refrigerator, freezer, or bathroom cabinet, and you're likely to find a Unilever product.

In the 1890s, William Hesketh Lever, founder of Lever Bros., wrote down his ideas for Sunlight Soap--his revolutionary new product that helped popularize cleanliness and hygiene in Victorian England. His idea was "to make cleanliness commonplace; to lessen work for women; to foster health and contribute to personal attractiveness, that life may be more enjoyable and rewarding for the people who use our products." This was long before the phrase "Corporate Mission" had been invented, but these ideas have continued to guide the practices of Unilever ever since, even if Lever's language and the notion of only women doing housework has become outdated.

In the late 19th century, the businesses that would later become Unilever were among the most philanthropic of their time. They set up projects to improve the lot of their workers and created products with a positive social impact, making hygiene and personal care commonplace and improving nutrition through adding vitamins to foods that were already daily staples. Today, Unilever still believes that success means, as its corporate principles state, acting with "the highest standards of corporate behavior towards our employees, consumers and the societies and world in which we live." Over the years the company has launched or participated in an ever-growing range of initiatives to source sustainable supplies of raw materials, protect environments, support local communities, and much more.

description: CLARK'S CUBES, COMMITTED TO A SUSTAINABLE AND CONVENIENT LIFESTYLE

While working in the bottled beverage industry, our founder, Chris Clark, frequently noticed how everyone uses and loves coffee pods, bottled drinks, powder packets, etc. Unfortunately, all of those convenient options come in wasteful plastic containers.
Chris began experimenting in his kitchen
to create a delicious, convenient, and sustainable option for himself and others while preventing plastic packaging waste from entering the already overflowing waste stream
. Clark's Cubes were born.
They're just as easy to prepare as coffee pods or drink packets but without the waste contributing to micro-plastics and our ocean trash islands
. They're way easier than brewing drip coffee or steeping tea bags as well.
Just pull a cube out of the compostable corn-based seal inside your Travel Tin or Refill Box and Drop, Stir, Enjoy! Ready in 30 seconds or less hot, 3 minutes iced.
No mess. No fuss. No waste.

When we decided to share Chris's Clark's Cubes creation at community farmers markets and local grocery stores, our customers showed us that Clark's Cubes are not just an easy way to reduce plastic packaging, but they are also
perfect for backpacking, travel, replacing wasteful pods at the office or as a gift.
So this is we are all about: enjoy a sustainable and convenient lifestyle without leaving any trace behind.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description: About the Brand

Just Born is a family-owned candy manufacturer that has been in business for more than seven decades and three generations. They make everyone's favorite candies: Mike and Ike, Hot Tamales, Zours, Teenee Beanee Gourmet Jelly Beans, and seasonal Marshmallow Peeps.
Founder Sam Born

The Just Born candy tradition was conceived in 1910, when Sam Born immigrated to the United States from Russia. A candy maker by trade, Born was also ingenious in the use of technology. Inventing chocolate sprinkles, known as jimmies, and the hard chocolate coating on ice cream bars. In 1916, Born was given the keys to the city of San Francisco for inventing a machine that mechanically inserted sticks into lollipops.

Born opened a small candy-making and retail store in Brooklyn, NY, in 1923. Ever the entrepreneur, he proudly displayed in his store window an evolving line of daily-made candy, marketing its freshness in a sign that declared "just born." The original company logo showed a baby resting in a candy measuring scale. Soon after opening the Brooklyn store, Born invited his brothers-in-law, Irv and Jack Shaffer, to join him to market and sell his confections. The company thrived in spite of the Depression, and in 1932, Just Born moved its operations to an empty printing factory in Bethlehem, Penn.
The popular Mike and Ike candies were introduced in 1940.

Mike and Ike fruit-flavored chewy candies were introduced in 1940. Hot Tamales were introduced a decade later. description: Pennyroyal is an aromatic herb related to mint and is used extensively in aromatherapy and traditional herbalism. It has been used for medicinal purposes, and in colonial times, it was popular for repelling insects. The oil of the plant is extremely toxic, so it is most often consumed in the form of tea, which has a strong minty flavor and aroma. This method yields one 8-ounce cup of pennyroyal tea. Step 1 Bring 8 ounces of spring or distilled water to a boil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Remove from heat as soon as boiling is achieved to prevent excessive evaporation. Step 2 Place one teaspoon of dried pennyroyal in a coffee mug or other heat-proof drinking container. Pour the boiling water over the herbs. Allow the mixture to stand for 10-15 minutes. Step 3 Place a fine mesh strainer over the top of a second clean coffee mug. Pour the liquid through the strainer to separate from the herbs. Discard the spent pennyroyal in the garbage bin or compost pile. Step 4 Sweeten the pennyroyal tea with honey if desired. Stir well to combine until the honey is thoroughly dissolved. Drink the tea immediately while warm. Do not exceed 3 cups per day.

description: Rust red in color with a unique smoky flavor, Pimentón de La Vera, or smoked paprika, is a versatile seasoning used in countless Spanish recipes. Made from freshly harvested peppers smoked for 15 days over encina oak wood fires, this pimentón is slightly sweet tasting with an intense smoked flavor. It is this intense smoky flavor that sets it apart from the bland paprika found in most grocery stores. Sweet smoked paprika is a key ingredient in authentic paella. Beyond paella, it is an excellent spice to use for flavoring potatoes, stews and sauces. Sweet smoked paprika's smoky, intense flavor is also fantastic with roasted meats, chicken or fish. La Dalia is the original and best brand of Pimentón de La Vera, and they still use stone mills to create the finest, most flavorful smoked paprika in Spain. The peppers used to produce La Dalia Pimentón de la Vera are hand-harvested each year in early autumn. Just after harvesting, the peppers are sent to wooden smokehouses filled with the smoke of encina oak wood fires. For 15 days, the peppers are dried in this intense smoke. Once dried, La Dalia grinds the peppers on traditional granite millstones - resulting in a silky, rust-red paprika that is both deeply flavored and smoky. Founded in 1913, La Dalia was the first company to produce the famous smoked paprika of La Vera. For generations, this family owned company has produced the finest quality pimentón using traditional production methods. This Pimentón de La Vera is Denominación de Origen (D.O.) - assuring its quality and authenticity!

description: Product Description

Crunchies Freeze-Dried Pineapple is 100 percent real, great-tasting pineapple chunks. The only thing taken out of the pineapple through Crunchies' patented freeze-drying process is water. No additives, no preservatives. That means no added sugar, no oil, no sulphur. They're wheat-free, gluten-free, and GMO-free, but rich in fiber and nutrients. You can also add them to pancakes, cereal, yogurt, or ice cream. Veggies can be eaten as a snack or sprinkled over your salads, soups and side dishes for added vitamins and nutrients! Crunchies Food Company was established in response to the rapid and overwhelming demand for good-tasting and truly healthy natural snacks on the market. The Company sought to develop a line of pure foods that would blend the tasty fun of potato chips, but but still be completely free of the preservatives, added sugars, trans fats and excessive sodium that are so prevalent among many snack food products. The result was an innovative breakthrough in blending great taste with important nutrition: Crunchies® freeze-dried fruits and vegetables which have proven hugely appealing to everyone from school children to seniors and from health-concious parents to busy executives.
Brand Story

Founded in 1993, Crunchies Food Company began with a mission: to create a line of foods that was not only unique and innovative, but also healthy and great tasting. The company also wanted to ensure that whatever foods they used were grown and handled in a way that was good for the environment, too. From the very beginning, every part of the company's process, including the packaging, literature, food-stuffs, employees, and the commitment to give back to the community, had to reflect the company's overarching philosophy.

Starting with reduced fat granolas with dried cherries and low-fat pancake mixes with orange zest and cardamom, and branching out into trail mixes made with unique organic and conventional fruits, Crunchies Food Company soon made a name for itself in California. But it wasn't until they discovered the uniqueness and healthfulness of freeze-dried fruits and vegetables that they really began to plan for a national expansion. Presently, Crunchies has made their way into some 700 stores nationwide and have been acknowledged by the likes of Bon Appetite, Fitness Magazine, Sports Illustrated for Women, and over a dozen other periodicals. They were also honored by their peers with an award for having one of the most innovative businesses in Central California.

description: Product Description

100% made from all-natural fruit, this is 25 wild-harvested, acai berries smooshed (with love!) with other whole fruits to take fruit snacks to a whole new, healthy and delicious level! And, oh, did we mention it’s helping to protect the Amazon Rainforest? Yeah, this is what fruit snacks should be.
From the Manufacturer
Made the right way.

Our fruit helps to protect the Amazon Rainforest and empower the people who live there. Our snacks are produced, by hand and with love, as part of a full wage employment program for people with disabilities in Ohio.
Made from the right stuff.

Fruit snacks made from fruit. 100%, all-natural, fruit-only. No sugar, flavorings, thickeners, or anything else added. Really. And the main ingredient? Superfood acai, packed with the power of the Amazon. And packed into, let us add, a compostable, non-plastic wrapper!
Convenient
A healthy, on-the-go snack to keep you energized.
Sustainable
Supports conservation and friendly development in the Amazon Rainforest.
Delicious
Our blends of exotic and familiar fruit gives just enough sweetness for a tasty treat anyone will feel good about enjoying - for so many reasons.
A snack to enjoy with peace of mind.

We wanted snacks that we could feel good about - from beginning to end - and that's what we've made for you. Nothing but naturally-delicious fruit, harvested to help the rainforest, and produced by hand to create jobs for people with disabilities in Ohio. Finally relax - this one is guilt free.
About the Startup
Describe your product in 3 words.
Simple. Sustainable. Superfood.
How did you come up with the idea for this product?

After serving as a Peace Corps Volunteer in the Amazon Rainforest, founder Evan Delahanty wanted a snack that would keep him connected to the vitality of Mother Nature. When he couldn't find one, he set out to make it.
What makes your product special?
Acai is more than a gimmick to us - it's our main ingredient! That's so you can taste and enjoy this awesome super-fruit, and also feel good about the positive impact you are having in the Amazon!
What has been the best part of your startup experience?
It feels good to be able to totally control the process, ensuring everything is done the right way for consumers, producers, and the planet!

description: Paradise Fruit Company was incorporated in 1961 as part of Canaveral Utilities and Development Co., a land development operation on the east coast of Florida. The name "Paradise", a label used by a company that had been in the 'glace' (candied) fruit business since the end of WW2, was acquired by Canaveral during the year of incorporation. After several acquisitions and mergers with similar businesses, 'glace' fruit became the major segment of the company's business. In 1965, the name was changed to Paradise Fruit Company, Inc. During those years, there were a number of relatively small operations manufacturing candied fruit, primarily for sale to commercial bakers. The management of Paradise anticipated that there was a great potential for direct sales to homemakers through supermarkets. Over a period of several years, Paradise developed the now familiar transparent, reusable plastic containers found in almost every supermarket during the holiday season. In order to become more immediately responsive to its customers needs, the company invested in a facility to manufacture all of its packaging. This, combined with large inventories, enabled almost overnight filling and shipping of orders. During the same period, the company acquired, merged with, or was licensed by a number of competitors to become the leading marketer of 'glace' fruit products under labels that have been trusted and asked for by customers for generations. Given the increasing diversification, the name of the company was changed to Paradise, Inc. in 1993. Paradise remains an innovator in 'glace' fruit marketing, introducing in 2003 a new package design that incorporates recipes and a cash-redeemable coupon.

In 1925, Rinaldo and Ezilda Torre visited family in Lucca, Italy. The popularity of specialty beverages and the support of cafés, restaurants and retailers have helped grow the Torani brand for the last 80 years. description: Also referred to as Piper longum, Pippali, Bengal Pepper, Indonesian Long Pepper, Java Pepper, Lada Panjong, and Bi Bo. The long pepper has been used for centuries in Mediterranean, African, Indian, and Indonesian cooking, although it has almost fallen into obscurity in the past few hundred years. The long pepper comes from a flowering vine with large catkin flowers. Within each flower are small black spikes that are the actual pepper. The taste is very similar to regular black pepper, and it is a relative of the species piper nigrum, but with a much hotter taste and an almost earthy, sweet overtone. It has been reported that Attila the Hun demanded part of the ransom for his sacking of Rome to be paid in long peppers. One of the most notable uses is as an ingredient in herbal medicine includes adding long pepper with ginger and black pepper in a popular base ingredient in Ayurvedic medicine called Trikatu.

About the Brand

Pringles, which first launched in October 1968, makes its unique snacks using dried potatoes that are cooked and mashed with just enough water and other wholesome ingredients added to form a smooth potato dough. Then, the dough is cut and placed on Pringle-shaped carriers (for that one-of-a-kind shape), fried, and seasoned just right on one side. Then, using special equipment, they're stacked into the unique Pringles cans.

The Pringles name came about in the late 1960s, when the company made a list of street names from a Cincinnati phone book that began with "P." Pringle Avenue in Finneytown was available for trademark, and its sound appealed to the brand.

The first Pringles were packaged in a tall, cylindrical metal can with a red wrapper. The brand expanded nationally in May 1975. Many different flavors and varieties came and went in the 1970s and 1980s, but the most significant breakthrough occurred in September 1996 with the launch of Fat Free Pringles, with P&G's olestra fat substitute.
Pringles is a member of the Proctor & Gamble family of brands.

About Proctor & Gamble Two billion times a day, Proctor & Gamble brands touch the lives of people around the world. The company has one of the largest and strongest portfolios of trusted brands in the world, including Pampers, Tide, Ariel, Always, Pantene, Bounty, Folgers, Pringles, Charmin, Downy, Iams, Crest, Actonel, and Olay.

It all started in 1837 when William Procter and James Gamble settled in Cincinnati. Procter quickly established himself as a candle maker, while Gamble apprenticed himself to a soap maker. The two might never have met had they not married sisters, Olivia and Elizabeth Norris, whose father convinced his new sons-in-law to become business partners. In 1837,a bold new enterprise was born: Procter & Gamble. By each pledging $3,596.47 to the new venture, they began selling soap and candles. Twenty-two years later, their business exceeded $1 million in sales. By 1980 that figure would reach $10 billion, and by 1993 the company would generate over $35 billion in revenue.

description: Many gardeners growing German White garlic declare it their favorite. Its claim to fame is the size of its cloves. The big bulbs have only four to six cloves, which makes them easier to peel. Exactly what is German White garlic? It’s an extremely popular type of hardneck garlic with ivory bulbs. The clove wrappers, however, are pink. This garlic is known by several other names. These include German Extra-Hardy, Northern White and German Stiffneck. These huge garlic bulbs have a rich, deep flavor with lasting heat. Are they spicy? They are, but not too much, just enough. This garlic softens and sweetens when it is cooked and is excellent in pesto, roasts and sauces. If you are considering growing German White garlic, you’ll be happy to hear that it stores well for a hardneck. You can leave it in cold storage and it will stay good until March or April.

Sumac is the star among the spices in Turkey and other Mediterranean countries. Similar to salt and pepper, sumac powder is often used for seasoning at the table.

Sumac has a particularly fruity, slightly tart and slightly sour taste. Therefore, sumac, similar to vinegar, is great for seasoning and ensures a pleasant acidity. But even when cooking sumac is a great spice! It refines meat and fish, bean and rice dishes or oriental dips. Sprinkle sumac over lettuce or combine it with parsley, sesame, garlic and cilantro to add that extra twist to your dishes!

Base spice in the Mediterranean with fruity, slightly tart and slightly sour flavors. The Romans appreciated sumac for its sour taste which made if perfect for BBQs, marinades, fish, meat and kebab dishes and even for yogurt sauces!

description: Edible Cake topper image 1/4 sheet frosting sheet, if you would like to add a personalized message please send me a message after the topper is purchased. How should I store my image? Store your image in the original bag in a cool, dry place at room temperature. Preparing your cake, if your icing is dry either add a little bit of water to your icing or if you have frozen icing spray your cake with a spray bottle and mist the top of the iced cake before applying the image lightly. DO NOT SPRAY THE IMAGE AS THE COLORS WILL START TO RUN. Images are best applied to light color icing, dark colors will make it hard for the image to be visible. Remove image from bag once ready to use and place it in the freezer for 10 to 20 seconds (It may peel off the backing without putting in the freezer) Remove the paper backing after freezing for 10 to 20 seconds and apply image to iced cake immediately. Applying your image Hold the photo gently at the edges and place in the middle onto the cake first. If any bubbles or wrinkles appear gently pat them out with clean dry fingers. If you accidently tear the image DO NOT PANIC! Just rub gently with dry fingers and it will disappear once the image starts to merge with the ice cake. The image will start to merge with icing immediately but it can take up to 3 hours to completely merge into the icing. It just depends how moist your icing is.Ice Cream Cakes If applying to an ice-cream cake apply the image directly onto the ice-cream cake top.

Founded by Lindsay Frucci, a self-proclaimed brownieholic, is dedicated to making brownie mix without fat, preservatives, or artificial ingredients
description: My name is Lindsay Frucci and I am a brownieholic. I love thick, fudgy, chewy brownies. I hate fat. In my food or on my hips, fat is something I like to live without. Since most thick, fudgy, chewy brownies are loaded with fat this created quite a problem. Were brownies without guilt a possibility? In January of 1995, I decided to try and find out. Since my family and I had already tried and rejected several commercially available fat free brownies (they either tasted like fruit or had no taste at all), I decided to see if I could come up with my own fat free brownie recipe. During the next few weeks, I made and threw away more pans of brownies than most people make in a lifetime. Fortunately, we were having some remodeling done on our home at the time and the two builders who were doing the work were only too happy to be my "official" taste testers. They took their mission very seriously, carefully evaluating every batch of fat free brownies for taste and texture. By the time the remodeling was done, I had a recipe for fat free brownies that were chewy, very rich and fudgy, and, best of all, FAT FREE I knew that I wanted to turn the recipe into a company, but with a background that included pediatric nursing and being a Mom, I had absolutely no idea how... Enter my local SCORE (Service Corps of Retired Executives) office. There, I was incredibly lucky to be connected with two wonderful gentlemen who had had extensive experience in the food industry. With their expertise and guidance, No Pudge! Foods was begun. FAT FREE Original Fudge Brownie Mix first appeared on the shelves of a few New Hampshire stores in August of 1995.

title: Aquatic Arts 5 Live Vampire Shrimp / Viper Shrimp | Freshwater Aquarium Filter Shrimp | Safe in Tetra / Guppy / Betta Fish Tanks
features: Vampire Shrimp are living, automatic aquarium filters - they use feather-like claspers to feed by filtering particles floating in the flow of your aquarium’s water currents.
These unique shrimp can change colors, ranging from a deep, silvery blue down to a russet brown. Their heads are topped with long antennae used to feel their way around a dark tank.
Similar to Singapore Flower Shrimp in that they are extremely peaceful and filter water particles. However, these shrimp grow larger than Singapore Flower Shrimp.
These are MUCH larger than dwarf shrimp, growing up to 5 to 6 inches. Fill your tank with culture plants or décor, as they do best in a tank that supports their tendency to hide and perch.
All Aquatic Arts brand plants and animals come with a 100% live arrival guarantee and free email support! We thoroughly inspect each shrimp before shipping to ensure they arrive alive and healthy.
description: Vampire Shrimp (Atya gabonensis) are among the most fascinating and unique aquarium animals available. Also known as African Filter Shrimp, Viper Shrimp, Gabon Shrimp, and Cameroon Shrimp, this giant but peaceful species is rare, but ideal for nano and planted aquariums. They have highly variable blue, silver gray, brown, white, or pink coloration that can change several times per year. They look especially neat with creative tank decorations; for example, their alien like appearance is perfect in a space themed aquarium with a galaxy background and robot props! Unlike many shorter-lived shrimp, the Vampire Shrimp can live for as long as 5 years with proper care! The Vampire Shrimp is a filter feeding creature and uses its appendages to pull microorganisms other fine food items from the water. In aquariums with multiple specimens, it is fun to see several of these shrimp gathered in one area feeding together. They are completely safe for dwarf shrimp aquariums, but do not tolerate temperatures as low as the temperatures that most dwarf shrimp enjoy. Vampire Shrimp require a heated aquarium with oxygen rich water and a heavier current than many other shrimp species. Providing places under which to hide, such as the leaves of live plants, is necessary for their long-term well-being. They can often be found toward the back of the tank, hanging or perching on fixtures such as an internal mag pump, filter, or temperature gauge. This shrimp needs brackish water to breed, so breeding in a home aquarium is nearly impossible.
CARE GUIDELINES:
- KH: 3 - 10 dKH
- Minimum tank size: 20 gallons
- Average adult size: 5 - 6 inches (12.7 - 15.2 cm)
- Average purchase size: 1 - 3 inches (2.5 - 7.6 cm)
